Separated from the Nile valley by the Red Sea Hills; Suakin looked to the Red Sea and Arabia (Holt & Daly, intro pp.1, 6).

Key events
  • Blemmyes (GHA II: 'customarily identified with the Bedja tribes') raid Upper Egypt; suppressed under Probus (276–282 CE)
  • After Meroe's fall the Nobades push the Blemmyes ('Bega or Buga') into the eastern desert
  • Recognised by medieval Muslim writers as distinct from Nubians, Arabs and 'Sudan'
  • Camel-nomads of the Red Sea Hills; gradual Islamisation and varying arabisation
  • Nabtab ruling clan of the Banu 'Amir claims Ja'ali descent
  • 'Ababda (north) Arabic-speaking; 18th c. southward expansion; Hadendowa in Taka (Gash) by early 19th c.
About the people
  • After Meroe's fall the Nobades push the Blemmyes ('Bega or Buga') into the eastern desert (G. Mokhtar (ed.), UNESCO International Scientific Committee (1981) General History of Africa, II: Ancient Civilizations of Africa, p.326)
  • Recognised by medieval Muslim writers as distinct from Nubians, Arabs and 'Sudan' (P.M. Holt & M.W. Daly (2011) A History of the Sudan: From the Coming of Islam to the Present Day, p.1)
  • Camel-nomads of the Red Sea Hills; gradual Islamisation and varying arabisation (P.M. Holt & M.W. Daly (2011) A History of the Sudan: From the Coming of Islam to the Present Day, p.6)
  • Nabtab ruling clan of the Banu 'Amir claims Ja'ali descent (P.M. Holt & M.W. Daly (2011) A History of the Sudan: From the Coming of Islam to the Present Day, p.4)
  • 'Ababda (north) Arabic-speaking; 18th c. southward expansion; Hadendowa in Taka (Gash) by early 19th c. (P.M. Holt & M.W. Daly (2011) A History of the Sudan: From the Coming of Islam to the Present Day, pp.6–7)

Culture

Islamised, with varying arabisation, often limited to claiming an Arab pedigree (Holt & Daly, intro p.6).

Economy

Camel nomadism; some sedentarisation linked to the modern Gash and Tokar agricultural schemes (Holt & Daly, intro p.6).

Peoples

  • Beja: Red Sea Hills hinterland behind 'Aydhab, Badi' and Suakin [medium] · control
    275 CE – present

    Nomadic Beja held the hinterland; with no centralized organization, treaties with Muslim Egypt covered only some groups.

    Not mapped: no gazetteer anchor for this place in the cited source; no source gives limits

    Sources: M. El Fasi and I. Hrbek, Stages in the development of Islam and its dissemination in Africa, ch.3 (General History of Africa III) (1988), p.82

  • Beja homeland: Suakin APPROXIMATE homeland

    Red Sea Hills and their hinterland, from the Red Sea littoral inland; settled Bisharin on the Atbara River, settled Hadendowa near Tokar, Bani Amir along the border with northern Ethiopia/Eritrea. Anchor point only; text only; no source gives limits.

    wikidata:Q571215 · Wikidata P625

  • Beja homeland: Tokar APPROXIMATE homeland

    Red Sea Hills and their hinterland, from the Red Sea littoral inland; settled Bisharin on the Atbara River, settled Hadendowa near Tokar, Bani Amir along the border with northern Ethiopia/Eritrea. Anchor point only; text only; no source gives limits.

Relations

AllianceConflictTradeSubjugationMigration

  • Beja → Muslim Egypt Conflict SINGLE-SOURCE [medium]

    Beja incursions harassed Upper Egypt for a long time; Muslim governments answered with treaties like the one with the Nubians.

    No arrow: no anchor for "Muslim Egypt"

    Sources: M. El Fasi and I. Hrbek, Stages in the development of Islam and its dissemination in Africa, ch.3 (General History of Africa III) (1988), p.82

  • Beja → Arab nomadic groups Migration REPORTED [medium]

    Arab nomadic groups moved into Beja country and intermarried with Beja ruling families; their children became chiefs of some Beja groups. The contacts did not end in complete fusion.

    No arrow: no anchor for "Arab nomadic groups"

    Sources: M. El Fasi and I. Hrbek, Stages in the development of Islam and its dissemination in Africa, ch.3 (General History of Africa III) (1988), p.82; L. Kropáček, Nubia from the late 12th century to the Funj conquest in the early 16th century, ch.16 (General History of Africa IV) (1984), p.412

Dating note

Start c.275 CE = earliest dated Blemmyes activity in GHA II ch.7 (Probus 276–282). The Blemmyes=Beja equation is customary, NOT proven (GHA II ch.10); GHA II ch.11 says earlier Meroitic-era Majai/Reheres 'could have been' Beja ancestors, so earlier origins are possible. Ongoing people, not a polity.

أحداث رئيسية
  • البليميون (تاريخ أفريقيا العام، المجلد الثاني: «يُطابَقون عادةً مع قبائل البجة») يغيرون على صعيد مصر؛ قُمعوا في عهد بروبوس (276–282 م)
  • بعد سقوط مروي دفع النوباديون البليميين («البجة أو البوجة») إلى الصحراء الشرقية
  • ميّزهم الكتّاب المسلمون في العصور الوسطى عن النوبة والعرب و«السودان»
  • رعاة إبل رحّل في تلال البحر الأحمر؛ أسلمة تدريجية وتعريب متفاوت
  • النابتاب، العشيرة الحاكمة لبني عامر، يدّعون النسب الجعلي
  • العبابدة (في الشمال) يتحدثون العربية؛ توسع نحو الجنوب في القرن الثامن عشر؛ والهدندوة في التاكا (القاش) بحلول مطلع القرن التاسع عشر يحتاج تحقق

  • النابتاب، العشيرة الحاكمة لبني عامر، يدّعون النسب الجعلي (P.M. Holt & M.W. Daly (2011) A History of the Sudan: From the Coming of Islam to the Present Day, p.4)
